欢迎来到sprawling v0.0.15 Alpha 261102 （HENCEFORTH）！
本版依旧为少量细微更新，稍微值得说道的只有将字体从Geist Mono换成了Maple Mono，后者提供官方带CJK的版本（并未内置，因为CJK字符集合起来比项目本体大几倍）可以给需要CJK的用户提供更好的阅读一致性，同时让整体的视觉风格暖了很多，后续再在设置里补上更细的字体设置。同时这个版本的修改动到了内核，同时大面积涉及了其它重要的包，不免又会出现一些新的Bug似乎也可以预见。由于个人精力和经济双重陷入严重困境，11月上旬更新会更加缓慢，大量优化（任务成功率，前端表现，更多性能优化，智能缓存优化，安全和隐私更新，优化的版本控制，性能测量，持久化，全面测试……）或在11月下旬到下个月初来到。
不同模型间的代码质量差异巨大，有些模型的代码几乎可以说是“有毒”，CI全绿也不应该合并，但我又不想加上一个模型歧视政策（比如说名称带Flash的模型提交自动Close，或者[CursorBench](https://cursor.com/cn/cursorbench)与[FrontierCode](https://cognition.com/frontiercode)得分少于X的模型提交自动Close，甚至在Action里检查模型指纹非Claude/GPT直接Close，不过就目前格局来说差不多是一件事），目前我准备对那些明显不用心+质量不满足合并条件的PR打上AI slop标签。2026年的软件开发是个门槛在减低但依然很高的事情，它的投入-产出并非一条直线提升，而是更接近于有一点偏移在大概30-50$达到0的对数曲线。用很便宜的模型工作就不应该超出用Python开发一次性工具，昂贵的模型就可以更多用于开发完整的Rust应用。如果三个月前我知道这条路线的经济-精力成本如此之高，而我的承受能力是这个情况，我无论如何都不会选择这一条技术路线。最近的开发主力已经从Claude Opus 5.5完全转向了Kimi K3.1 Pro，Kimi一直是我最喜欢的开源模型，但它依然有过于昂贵和缓慢的问题，而且真实任务中二者成本差不多。当然，Claude依然并且未来将一直是SOTA模型，但Kimi也有一些额外的好处，尤其是相对适合我当前的场景少量使用。自sprawling v0.0.13 Alpha 261026 (ODYSSEY)之后，无论是Commit的量还是Release Note的技术讨论都少了很多。归根结底就是没什么值得讨论的东西了，甚至我认为现在不少人大谈特谈的东西在几个月前就已经有比现在他们的设想更成熟的实现。这当然是个好事，接触Agent的人越来越多，但另外一边也的确就没什么创新，比如说这个项目[dsh-superagent-prototype](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype)。值得讨论的我都讨论过了，所以对这个也没什么需要额外说的。如果我现在有无限的Claude额度把剩下的功能做完，实际上我也不知道要做什么，只是出于经济我没办法无限使用Claude，只好等Opus5.5级别的智能变得普惠。Agent的核心还是Model，好的模型即使被拖后腿依然能高质完成任务，差的模型怎么约束和引导都没用，无非是直接失败和运行时投毒的细微差别。我在考虑今年12月或明年1月将前端完整迁移至[Leptos](https://github.com/leptos-rs/leptos)同时放弃完全生成式UI方案转向部分生成式UI，具体取决于模型的进步速度与前端完善程度(Rust前端开发最麻烦的肯定还是视觉检查需要漫长等待，但如果前端已经用Svelte完成了实现，剩下只是单纯追求性能表现和逻辑清晰度时构建缓慢就不再是问题了），当然更主要取决于我对UI/UX的学习和思考。只要情况好转，希望在月末或下月能扭转这种情况，我会尽可能加大对项目的投入回到快速开发和完善的阶段中。我知道现在项目还不够好，但至少再困难也不至于放弃开发。不过拖太久我也不担心会是坏事，看到AI能力指数增张的趋势，现在我们面对的99%难题可能在3-6个月之内被解决，然后在6-9个月内将成本压倒一半以内，12-15个月之后说不定就算我想用Zig（或其他语言）重写整个项目或对项目的全部代码进行深入底层的优化（毕竟现在的确有很多愚蠢的slop code）都用不到现在我一个月生活费。也许现在Code依然没有被解决，但谁又像一年前（严格来说是11个月前）那样坚定地对着Opus4.5带来的变革说Code不会被解决。
欢迎来帮助开发项目，ゆっくりしていってね！！！

**In English / 英文版**

Welcome to sprawling v0.0.15 Alpha 261102 (HENCEFORTH)!
This release is again a small one; the only change worth mentioning is the reading font moving from Geist Mono to Maple Mono. The latter offers an official CJK build (not bundled, since the CJK character set is several times larger than the project itself), which gives users who read CJK better reading consistency and warms up the whole visual style; finer font settings will follow in the settings later. This release also touches the kernel and, across the board, several other important packages, so a few new bugs are, perhaps, foreseeable. With both my energy and my budget in serious difficulty, updates will be slower in the first third of November; a large batch of optimisation work (task success rate, frontend behaviour, more performance, smart caching, security and privacy, improved version control, performance measurement, persistence, full testing...) may arrive from late November into early December.
The code-quality gap between models is enormous; some models' code is almost "poisonous", and a fully green CI is not a reason to merge. I still do not want a model-discrimination policy (for example, auto-closing submissions from models with "Flash" in the name, or from models scoring below X on [CursorBench](https://cursor.com/cn/cursorbench) or [FrontierCode](https://cognition.com/frontiercode), or even checking in Actions for a model fingerprint that is not Claude/GPT — though given the current landscape these amount to nearly the same thing). For now I intend to label pull requests that are clearly careless and fail the quality bar for merging as AI slop. Software development in 2026 is a field whose threshold is lowering but still high: its input-output curve is not a straight line but closer to a logarithmic one, offset a little, that crosses zero somewhere around 30–50 dollars. Working with very cheap models should not go beyond one-off Python tooling, while expensive models can carry more of the work of building a complete Rust application. Had I known three months ago that the economic and energy cost of this path would be this high, and that my capacity was what it is, I would not have chosen this technical route at all. The main development model has now fully shifted from Claude Opus 5.5 to Kimi K3.1 Pro. Kimi has long been my favourite open model, but it remains too expensive and too slow, and in real tasks the two cost about the same. Claude is, of course, and will remain, the SOTA model; but Kimi has extra advantages too, especially suiting my current scenario in small doses. Since sprawling v0.0.13 Alpha 261026 (ODYSSEY), both the volume of commits and the technical discussion in the release notes have shrunk a lot. The root cause is that little is left worth discussing; I would even say that much of what many people now talk about at length already had a more mature implementation months ago than what they now imagine. That is, of course, a good thing — more and more people are coming into contact with Agents — but on the other side there really is little innovation. Take this project, [dsh-superagent-prototype](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype): I have discussed everything I found worth discussing, so there is nothing more to add on this one. If I had unlimited Claude quota to finish the remaining features, I would not actually know what to build; it is only economics that stops me from using Claude without limit, so I must wait for Opus-5.5-class intelligence to become affordable to all. The core of an Agent is still the Model: a good model completes tasks at high quality even when held back, while a poor model is beyond constraint and guidance — the difference is merely between failing outright and poisoning the runtime. I am considering moving the frontend wholesale to [Leptos](https://github.com/leptos-rs/leptos) in December this year or January next, leaving the fully generative UI approach for a partly generative one — depending on the pace of model progress and the state of the frontend (the most tedious part of Rust frontend development is surely the long waits for visual checks, but once the frontend is already implemented in Svelte and the remaining goal is purely performance and clarity of logic, slow builds stop being the problem), and of course depending above all on my own UI/UX learning and thinking. As long as things improve, I hope to reverse this slowdown by the end of this month or next, and to put as much as I can back into fast development and refinement. I know the project is not good enough yet, but however hard it gets, abandoning development is not on the table. Nor am I worried that a long delay would be a bad thing: looking at the trend of AI capability growing exponentially, 99% of the problems we face now may be solved within 3–6 months; the cost may be halved within 6–9 months; and 12–15 months from now, perhaps even rewriting this entire project in Zig (or another language), or deeply optimising all of its code down to the low level (there is, after all, quite a lot of stupid slop code now), would cost less than one month of my living expenses. Maybe Code is not solved yet, but who would now say, as firmly as they did a year ago (strictly speaking, eleven months ago, after the change Opus 4.5 brought), that Code will not be solved.
Welcome to help develop the project, and ゆっくりしていってね！！！

**Notes / 补充**

- **Known issue / 已知问题** — ([#185](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/issues/185)) On an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, forking a session containing tool calls fails. The Ledger redacts the provider's tool call id as `secret:redacted/<hash>` because of its key-like shape, and the rebuilt history sends it back unchanged; Anthropic requires an id matching `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, answers 400, and the run ends cancelled. Version 0.0.14 behaves the same way, and the proposed fix in [#189](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/pull/189) is not included in this release. An OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepts the id, and a new session is unaffected.

  （[#185](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/issues/185)）在 Anthropic 兼容格式的端点上，分叉一个含工具调用的会话会失败。账本把 provider 给的 tool call id 按密钥形状抹成 `secret:redacted/<hash>`，重建历史时原样发出，Anthropic 要求 id 匹配 `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`，回答 400，run 以 cancelled 结束。0.0.14 也是这样；[#189](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/pull/189) 的候选修复没有包含在本版中。OpenAI 兼容格式的端点接受这个 id，新会话不受影响。

**What comes next** — slower updates through the first third of November, then a batch of optimisation work (task success rate, frontend behaviour, more performance, caching, security and privacy, version control, measurement, persistence, full testing) aimed at late November to early December; a wholesale frontend move to Leptos is under consideration for December or January. No version or date is promised for `v0.1.0` Beta, and finishing any item here does not by itself make it.
